Campaign_Map_And_Navigation.cloudColor: Defines the base RGBA rendering tint for procedural background nebula clouds within the hyperspace overworld and localized star system deep-space backgrounds. Interacts heavily with standard alpha compositing to create dense, navigable gas fields.
Campaign_Map_And_Navigation.noiseColor: Controls the chromatic tint and opacity of the static grain texture algorithm applied directly over nebular clouds. This procedural noise layer is essential for generating the illusion of volumetric depth and atmospheric turbulence within hyperspace.
Campaign_Map_And_Navigation.asteroidBeltMapColor: Governs the rendering opacity and primary hue of the orbital bands drawn on the strategic macro-map interface to signify the physical presence of asteroid fields. Ensures the player can visually navigate away from transit-slowing phenomena.
Campaign_Map_And_Navigation.ringSystemMapColor: Dictates the visual representation of planetary and solar ring systems on the macro-map. This variable works in tandem with float bandwidth arrays, such as bandWidthInTexture, to simulate varying densities of dust and ice particulates orbiting celestial bodies.
Campaign_Map_And_Navigation.iconWaypointColor: The primary indicator color for user-plotted astrogation courses. It renders the projected travel path vectors and destination chevrons on the sector map, providing immediate optical feedback regarding the fleet's trajectory and fuel range.
Campaign_Map_And_Navigation.iconFriendColor: The semiotic signifier for allied vessels and infrastructure on the strategic radar. The engine pulls this variable when the polled diplomatic integer between the player and the target entity exceeds the defined allied threshold.
Campaign_Map_And_Navigation.iconEnemyColor: The absolute indicator for hostile fleets and stations. This variable visually overrides all other factional or neutral colors on the radar when the diplomatic integer falls below the hostility threshold, ensuring the player is instantly aware of intercepting threats.
Campaign_Map_And_Navigation.iconNeutralShipColor: The baseline radar blip color for non-affiliated, non-hostile entities navigating the sector map. Typically applied to independent scavengers, unaligned traders, and mercenary patrols lacking a formal diplomatic standing with the player.

User_Interface_And_HUD.buttonBg: The foundational background variable for all interactive menu elements. It defines the resting state opacity and primary tint of standard UI buttons across the Tripad operating system, heavily relying on alpha blending to allow the starry background to bleed through.
User_Interface_And_HUD.buttonBgDark: A supplementary rendering variable used to generate drop-shadows, recessed paneling, and the visual simulation of three-dimensional depth beneath active UI frames, preventing the interface from appearing entirely flat.
User_Interface_And_HUD.buttonText: The primary typographical variable governing the font color of unselected, standard interactive text within the Tripad interface. Usually set to a high-contrast white or light gray to ensure readability against the dark backgrounds.
User_Interface_And_HUD.buttonShortcut: A high-visibility chromatic tag applied specifically to keystroke characters embedded within button text. By highlighting the hotkey (e.g., 'R' for Refit), this variable draws user attention to efficient keyboard inputs, increasing the player's potential actions per minute.
User_Interface_And_HUD.widgetBorderColorDark: Forms the exterior dark bevel of pop-up windows, dialog boxes, and inventory frames. It creates a distinct structural boundary against the stellar background, defining the physical edge of the diegetic Tripad screen.
User_Interface_And_HUD.widgetBorderColorBright: Provides the interior light catch for the UI beveling system. It works in direct tandem with the dark border to simulate physical screen casing and window depth, completing the retro-futuristic aesthetic.
User_Interface_And_HUD.standardUIIconColor: The uniform variable applied to generic, non-diegetic interface iconography, such as settings gears, exit crosses, and pagination arrows. Ensures that functional UI elements do not visually conflict with diegetic narrative elements or item sprites.
User_Interface_And_HUD.tripadGridColor: Defines the background hex and square tiling matrix rendered behind the intelligence, codex, and fleet management screens. This geometric tiling is fundamental to simulating the digital cathode-ray tube operating system of the game's universe.
User_Interface_And_HUD.tripadLineColor: Controls the opacity and hue of the horizontal scanlines overlaid across the UI background grids. By manipulating this variable's alpha channel, modders can directly increase or decrease the visual noise and technological motif of the interface.
User_Interface_And_HUD.tooltipTitleAndLightHighlightColor: A critical dual-purpose variable utilized to render the primary title headers of item tooltips and provide subtle glow effects behind critical data matrices, ensuring the user's eye is immediately drawn to the most important identifying information.

Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarCargoColor: The baseline status variable representing the utilization of the fleet's physical freight and commodity capacity. Scales linearly across the horizontal bar as the player fills their freighters with salvage, trade goods, and armaments.
Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarCrewColor: The status variable indicating the population levels of standard crew and marine contingents relative to maximum life support parameters. Essential for tracking the personnel necessary to deploy ships and conduct ground raids.
Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarFuelColor: The status variable tracking antimatter fuel reserves. This is a highly critical bar, as fuel is necessary for hyperspace astrogation and jump-point transitions; running empty leaves the fleet stranded in deep space.
Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarHullColor: The primary structural integrity metric, visually mapping the remaining physical armor and hull points of a vessel during real-time combat and within the refit screen. Usually defaults to a stable green or gray.
Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarCRColor: The visual representation of Combat Readiness. This tracks an abstract calculation of crew fatigue, supply maintenance, and systemic deployment capability, slowly degrading as the ship spends time deployed in the tactical grid.
Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarOverflowColor: A high-alert override variable triggered when logistical capacities (cargo, fuel, personnel) are exceeded. It warns the user of imminent resource loss, massive sensor profile penalties, or the active bleeding of physical goods into the void.
Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarWarningColor: The primary cautionary state variable (typically yellow or orange) triggered when structural integrity or Combat Readiness degrades past nominal safety thresholds, drawing optical attention without inducing immediate panic.
Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarDangerColor: The critical failure state variable (typically pure red) utilized when a vessel faces imminent destruction or catastrophic deployment malfunctions, signaling that weapons will jam and engines will flame out if not immediately addressed.
Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarFleetPointsColor: Tracks the expenditure of Deployment Points during the tactical pre-battle interface. It represents the logistical bandwidth and communication limits of the combat operation, preventing the deployment of infinite reinforcements.
Telemetry_And_Progress_Bars.progressBarHangarSpaceColor: Indicates the status and replacement rate capacity of fighter wing bays during real-time tactical engagements, allowing the player to visually track when a carrier has exhausted its chassis replacement components.

Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.mountYellowColor: The primary optical indicator on the refit wireframe denoting a Ballistic weapon hardpoint. This color strictly reserves the slot for kinetic and high-explosive ordnance, ensuring architectural parity during loadout construction.
Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.mountGreenColor: The primary optical indicator on the refit wireframe denoting an Energy weapon hardpoint. This color reserves the slot for plasma, beam, and pulse emission systems that rely heavily on the ship's flux dissipation network.
Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.mountBlueColor: The primary optical indicator on the refit wireframe denoting a Missile weapon hardpoint. This distinct color reserves the slot for self-propelled and guided payload delivery systems with limited ammunition capacities.
Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.mountGrayColor: An indicator denoting a Decorative or built-in chassis element. This signals to the user that the specific slot represents structural plating or an integrated hullmod that cannot be modified or removed during standard refit operations.
Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.mountOrangeColor: The optical indicator denoting a Composite hybrid hardpoint. Renders as a secondary blend to visually imply that the mount is capable of interfacing with either Ballistic or Missile ordnance, offering tactical flexibility.
Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.mountCyanColor: The optical indicator denoting a Synergy hybrid hardpoint. Renders as a secondary blend to visually imply that the mount is capable of interfacing with either Energy or Missile ordnance.
Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.fogOfWarColor: Governs the opacity and tint of the tactical map wash overlaying coordinates that lack allied sensor or radar coverage. This directly affects the player's spatial awareness, hiding enemy deployments until they breach sensor range.
Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.weaponArcColor: Draws the absolute maximum traverse boundaries of a weapon's turret or hardpoint mechanism on the tactical HUD and refit grids, projecting a geometric cone that defines the exact area of denial for that weapon system.
Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.weaponArcFFColor: A secondary arc rendering variable that adjusts the visual traverse boundaries to account for friendly-fire calculation parameters. It indicates the restricted zones where a weapon will actively refuse to fire to avoid striking an allied vessel.
Refit_Architecture_And_Combat.standardGridColor: The highly transparent, non-intrusive alignment matrix drawn beneath the tactical combat space. It provides essential visual scale and distance estimation for judging weapon ranges and intercept vectors without cluttering the screen.

Typography_And_Dialogue.hColor: The master typographical highlight variable, heavily utilized to draw attention to statistical integers, critical nouns, and positive modifiers within dense text blocks. It creates a skimmable interface, allowing rapid data extraction from complex tooltips.
Typography_And_Dialogue.textFriendColor: The relational font variable used to identify allied personnel, positive faction reputation shifts, and cooperative entities in the dialogue frame. Reinforces positive geopolitical interactions through green-spectrum visual feedback.
Typography_And_Dialogue.textEnemyColor: The relational font variable used to identify hostile targets, negative reputation shifts, and active threats. It mathematically overrides standard text colors when the diplomatic integer falls below zero, utilizing red-spectrum feedback.
Typography_And_Dialogue.textNeutralColor: The baseline font variable for unaligned, non-hostile entities, scavengers, and independent markets lacking a formal diplomatic standing. Represents interactions that carry no immediate geopolitical risk or reward.
Typography_And_Dialogue.flatRedTextColor: A stark warning highlight used within tooltips and dialogue to indicate severe statistical penalties, restricted actions, or mechanical degradation, such as applying a D-mod to a pristine ship hull.
Typography_And_Dialogue.yellowTextColor: A cautionary typographical highlight used for systemic alerts, suspicious dialogue choices, and mid-level mechanical warnings. Guides the player's attention toward potential risks without explicitly forbidding the action.
Typography_And_Dialogue.textGrayColor: A subdued font variable used for inactive dialogue options, purely narrative flavor text, historical lore, and non-critical environmental descriptors. Deprioritizes the text in the visual hierarchy.
Typography_And_Dialogue.storyOptionColor: A unique, highly saturated variable (specifically ) applied to dialogue choices requiring the expenditure of a Story Point. It signals a meta-narrative action that bypasses standard mechanical constraints, offering guaranteed success for a rare currency.

Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.designTypeColors: A master JSON array introduced in the 0.9a engine revision that assigns specific hues to tooltips and blueprint ledgers based on the technological origin or manufacturer of an item, enabling rapid visual sorting of industrial capacity and deep lore integration.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.tech_Common: The baseline design type color applied to standard, ubiquitous items lacking a specialized manufacturing origin. Represents universally accessible, unbranded technology.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.tech_LowTech: The design type color (typically rendering in rusty oranges or browns) applied to rugged, heavily armored, ballistic-focused vessels and armaments. Implies outdated but highly reliable surplus hardware.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.tech_Midline: The design type color (typically bright, warning yellows) applied to mass-produced, versatile, and highly mobile technological assets favored by independent syndicates and the Persean League.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.tech_HighTech: The design type color (typically clinical cyan or blue) applied to fragile, highly advanced assets reliant on massive shield capacities and energy projection, heavily associated with Tri-Tachyon corporate research.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.tech_Remnant: The design type color (teal or hostile purples) applied to hyper-advanced, strictly hostile artificial intelligence automated grids and structural fragments left over from the AI Wars.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.tech_Pirate: The design type color applied to jury-rigged, heavily modified, and illicitly obtained black-market technology. Implies compromised structural integrity in exchange for aggressive burst damage.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.tech_Unknown: The default fallback variable used when the engine cannot parse the manufacturer origin of a specific entity or modded asset, ensuring the tooltip does not crash the rendering pipeline.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.tech_DomainRestricted: The design type color applied to highly illegal, pre-collapse relic technologies and planet-killer scale armaments. Implies massive geopolitical consequences if deployed openly.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.secondaryUIColor: A specialized factional variable defining the color of the segmented, rotating secondary rings that encircle selected fleets or orbital stations on the macro-map. Allows factions to project a dual-color identity across their territorial footprint.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.faction_Hegemony: The specific hex variables applied to the martial, domain-successor state. Dominates their localized UI grids and fleet heraldry with a stark, uncompromising military orange.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.faction_LuddicPath: The variables defining the hostile, radical fundamentalist faction. Traditionally renders their user interface interactions and map footprint in aggressive, unrefined greens.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.faction_LuddicChurch: The variables defining the established, agrarian religious faction. Utilizes subdued, naturalistic UI color shifts to reflect their anti-industrial theology.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.faction_PerseanLeague: The variables defining the unified independent syndicates. Utilizes bold, standardized coloring for their territorial UI, reflecting their organized but fractured geopolitical nature.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.faction_LionsGuard: The specialized, elite factional variables utilized by the Sindrian Diktat's highest-tier military formations, separating the dictator's personal guard visually from standard planetary defense forces.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.manufacturer_FabriqueOrbitale: The exact design type color specifically mapped to blueprints and weaponry produced by the Fabrique Orbitale corporate entity, embedding their corporate branding directly into the UI.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.manufacturer_ExodyneBiotech: The design type color mapped to the advanced medical and biological assets of the Exodyne Biotech corporation, differentiating their outputs from standard hardware manufacturers.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.manufacturer_KoCombine: The design type color mapped to the heavy industrial and mining output of the Ko Combine manufacturing bloc.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.manufacturer_EridaniUtopia: The design type color mapped to pre-collapse terraforming equipment and specialized environmental armaments produced by the Eridani-Utopia Terraforming entity.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.manufacturer_MbayeGogol: The design type color mapped to the highly specialized corporate outputs of the Mbaye-Gogol entity, allowing for deep narrative tracking of their proprietary hardware.
Industrial_Taxonomy_And_Factions.manufacturer_BhilaiAstra: The design type color mapped to the specific ballistic and kinetic outputs of the Bhilai Astra manufacturing yards, distinguishing their weapons from generic low-tech variants.
